Top candidates: Charcoal_Stalk_Rot (tiny black sclerotia in pith), Diplodia_Stalk_Rot (pycnidia), Physoderma_Stalk_Rot.

Let me check reference images one at a time.
Charcoal Stalk Rot shows dark/black pith with tiny sclerotia when split open. The test image has specks on the outer surface. Let me check Diplodia_Stalk_Rot.
This Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference is visually very similar to the test image - broken stalk at node, tan color, similar setting. Let me check more to compare.
Now I need to cover more classes. Let me check the remaining stalk-related diseases and others.
Fusarium shows ear rot, not relevant. Continuing with more classes.
The Anthracnose image shows broken stalks at node with some pinkish discoloration - similar framing to test image but different coloring. Let me check more classes.

I've covered 17 classes. Now let me compare my top candidates more closely. The test image most closely resembles Diplodia_Stalk_Rot (broken stalk at node). Let me view the second Diplodia reference to confirm.

This confirms it. Diplodia_Stalk_Rot reference (Corn_Disease_20.jpg) shows the exact same tiny black specks (pycnidia) on a tan/cream stalk surface — identical to the test image. Combined with Corn_Disease_14.jpg showing the same broken-at-node stalk appearance and setting, this is a strong match.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: broken corn stalk at a node, tan/straw colored, with tiny black specks scattered on the outer surface, fibrous pith visible at the break
- Diplodia_Stalk_Rot matches on all features: broken stalk at node (Corn_Disease_14), tiny black pycnidia on tan stalk surface (Corn_Disease_20), same field setting
- Charcoal_Stalk_Rot shows black sclerotia primarily in split pith (darker, more interior), different from the surface specks in the test image
- All leaf diseases (NLB, rust, tar spot, etc.) are clearly not relevant
- All ear rots (Fusarium, Gibberella, Diplodia_Ear_Rot, Aspergillus) involve the ear, not the stalk
